requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturers need to show valid clinical association, analytical/technical validation and clinical validation; clinical validation follows analytical validation, applies to all risk classes, and is evaluated before market placement and after; example metrics include sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV.

clause_or_page: Overview, PDF p.2 (printed p.2); mapping, date and audiences from https://aiverifyfoundation.sg/tools/ai-verify-testing-framework/
requirement_paraphrase: Process-check framework to assess AI systems against 11 principles (transparency, explainability, reproducibility, safety, security, robustness, fairness, data governance, accountability, human agency and oversight, inclusive growth); each item has outcome, process and evidence, answered Yes/No/N/A with elaboration; mapped to NIST AI RMF, NIST GenAI Profile, Hiroshima Process code of conduct and ISO/IEC 42001.

Analytical validation should use a large independent reference dataset reflecting the intended purpose and population (prevalence, multi-centre sourcing, demographics, justified size, not publicly available), each requirement applying unless there is sufficient evidence that it need not be met; performance should be shown to generalise through multisite investigation and subgroup analysis, and be tested against a gold standard.

clause_or_page: Annexure C (AI Ethics Checklist), approx. pp. 41-46; layout scrambled in extraction, low confidence
requirement_paraphrase: Provides a lifecycle checklist (Plan and Design, Prepare Input Data, Build and Validate, Deploy and Monitor) with a column marking whether each item is binding for third parties.

clause_or_page: Policy statement 2.1.3, printed p.11; Implementation Guidance 3.1.3 (AI Supply Chain Security), printed p.20
requirement_paraphrase: The entity must identify, assess and manage cyber risks in the AI/ML supply chain. Guidance: regular security assessments of vendors, developers and other third parties should be run, or independent third-party assurance reports (e.g. SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001) or recognised certifications may be relied on; contracts should cover AI cyber security requirements.

Effects should be evaluated in clinically relevant conditions integrated into the clinical workflow, comparing clinicians with and without the device; manufacturers should locally validate devices developed and approved in other jurisdictions.

clause_or_page: s3 Recommended Protocol, Risk Evaluation and Treatment, Step 4 'Control Identification', printed p.6
requirement_paraphrase: Risk controls for AI systems are identified through review of safeguards, gap analysis and stakeholder consultation, and are tested through simulations or pilot studies before full implementation to confirm they reduce risk and support AI safety and reliability.

AI systems should be tested before deployment and regularly while in operation; measurement should include rigorous software testing and performance assessment with measures of uncertainty, benchmark comparisons and documented reporting of results.
Once the model is ready, it is evaluated against acceptance criteria to confirm readiness for deployment.

AI services must be secure and resilient and comply with Secure by Design principles and the Government Cyber Security Standard; build safeguards including security testing and, for generative AI, content filtering and validation checks.

Compare results with pre-defined thresholds then review failure cases; adjust thresholds only with documented evidence; break results down by sub-category and attack technique, quantify variance and confidence intervals across runs, and analyse failures qualitatively including faults in the LLM judge.

clause_or_page: Implementation Guidance 3.4.4 'Testing and Validation of AI/ML Systems', printed p.36 (parent policy statement 2.4.4, printed p.14)
requirement_paraphrase: The entity should keep a framework for testing and validating AI/ML systems so accuracy, reliability and performance meet defined criteria; all AI/ML systems should be rigorously tested before deployment for functionality, security and resilience, covering varied scenarios and edge cases.
Providers must consider whether the system is likely to adversely affect persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups.

clause_or_page: Principle 5, Build and Validate item 2, p. 22
requirement_paraphrase: Technical robustness requires rigorous testing, validation and re-assessment with oversight controls built into development; system integration test sign-off should involve relevant stakeholders.
A risk assessment must be done for all AI systems and related assets; risks are tracked in a register with assigned owners.

clause_or_page: Security > Practical recommendations: 'Applies to generative AI' (public-facing LLM chatbots; no automatic destructive or irreversible actions) and 'Applies to AI' (review enterprise access controls before deploying an AI tool)
requirement_paraphrase: Avoid putting LLM chatbots on public-facing government websites unless the risk of direct prompt injection is acceptable for the use case; prevent generative AI responses from automatically triggering destructive or irreversible actions without human review; review enterprise access controls before deploying AI tools.

clause_or_page: Implementation Guidance 3.1.4 (Change Management and Reporting), printed p.21; 3.2.3 (Patch Management), printed p.24; parent policy statements 2.1.4 (printed p.11) and 2.2.3 (printed p.12)
requirement_paraphrase: Manual changes to AI/ML models, algorithms, training data or configurations should be documented, reviewed, approved and tested in a secure environment before deployment, with a rollback plan where possible; patches and updates should be tested in a controlled environment before production.

Where independent review is needed, the clinical evaluation should as far as possible be reviewed by someone not significantly involved in development and with nothing to gain, proportionate to risk; an evaluation based on a comparator device must show clinical and technical equivalence including the algorithm.

Signatories define measurable systemic risk tiers or other acceptance criteria and proceed with development, release or use only if systemic risks are determined acceptable; otherwise they restrict, withdraw or recall and add mitigations.

clause_or_page: Outcome 7.2 / Process 7.2.1, p.72 (technical testing, generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Test for safety and possible harms against individuals or groups using benchmarks and red-teaming, document red-teamer instructions, and have stakeholders judge score acceptability.

Defines ten evaluation perspectives: toxic output control; misinformation and manipulation; fairness and inclusion; high-risk/unintended use; privacy; security; explainability; robustness; data quality; verifiability.

For MDMA the manufacturer is expected to provide technical documentation including product verification and validation; documentation should show verification against design specifications, validation that the device performs as intended, a usability study, and validation of safe performance under normal and reasonably foreseeable abnormal conditions.
Planned specification for quality assessment of prompt-based text-to-text generative AI systems, including safety assessment with red teaming; at stage 20.00 (registered Sept 2025).

clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Ethics > Fairness, bias and discrimination > Practical recommendations
requirement_paraphrase: Apply bias mitigation and fairness evaluation across the entire AI project life cycle; comply with human rights law, the Equality Act 2010, the Public Sector Equality Duty and EHRC guidance; review outputs and decisions for bias by measuring results for different groups, including intersectional groups; set up feedback routes for unfair decisions or harmful outputs; evaluate continuously as fairness expectations change.
Validation must include comprehensive testing across diverse datasets and contexts to confirm accuracy, safety and efficacy.

Connect measurement approaches to deployment context, informed by consultation with domain experts and other end users, and document them; inform measurement results on trustworthiness in deployment context and across the AI lifecycle with input from domain experts and relevant AI actors, to validate whether the system performs consistently as intended, and document results.

AI software and service providers register, appoint an AI officer, and complete a per-product questionnaire with supporting files on adherence to AI ethics standards; after committee review the product receives an incentive label and the provider an accreditation certificate.

DoH expects AI tools introduced in Abu Dhabi for healthcare delivery, public health, pharmaceutical production and medical research to be robust, evidenced by certification of the AI software (and of major upgraded versions) from recognised international agencies, compliance with ADSSSA regulations, and auditable validation statements.

clause_or_page: Using AI safely and responsibly > Data protection and privacy > Lawfulness and purpose limitation
requirement_paraphrase: The playbook says that before implementing AI solutions a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is needed; it cites UK GDPR Art. 35(3)(a) as requiring one where AI involves systematic automated evaluation with significant effects, large-scale special category processing or large-scale public monitoring, notes the ICO also requires one for innovative technology processing personal data, says the DPIA should cover each life-cycle stage including training and testing, and that the ICO must be consulted if high risk cannot be mitigated.

A new conformity assessment is required after a substantial modification; changes pre-determined at the initial assessment for continually learning systems and recorded in the technical documentation are not substantial modifications.
Tool for entities to compare their current practice against defined standards and obtain the level of ethical compliance of an AI model; links to the AI Ethics Principles.
All training data is filtered; assessment uses manual samples of at least 4,000 items (qualified rate at least 96%) and technical checks of at least 10% of volume (at least 98%).

Consider baseline benchmark performance when selecting a model; evaluate capability claims with empirically validated methods; share pre-deployment test results with actors holding release approval authority; use a purpose-built testing environment such as NIST Dioptra.

clause_or_page: Proposed Reg. 10.3.1(f) 'Safety', Annex A printed p.13; Consultation Paper para 18(b) and Q2
requirement_paraphrase: Proposed new design concept: a System must be designed, developed and operated with safeguards to identify use of personal data, assess and mitigate risks of harm to individuals, and intended to prevent discriminatory or biased outcomes through appropriate oversight, testing and controls.

Sandboxes give a controlled environment for development, training, testing and validation under an agreed sandbox plan; authorities give guidance and supervision to identify risks, and on request supply written proof and an exit report which market surveillance authorities and notified bodies must take positively into account.

All proprietary and third-party AI software must undergo formal secure code reviews and automated vulnerability scanning before deployment and during major updates, following recognised frameworks such as OWASP or NIST.
Operators are to identify and evaluate misuse risks (cyberattacks, fraud) and apply current techniques to reduce inappropriate outputs and malfunction.

Evaluations must assess the effectiveness of safety mitigations, including under adversarial pressure such as fine-tuning attacks or jailbreaking, and whether mitigations may be circumvented or degrade over time.

Planned technology-neutral guidance on red teaming of AI systems: terminology, risk and attack vector identification, planning and conducting assessments aligned with 29119, reporting, and lifecycle integration; at stage 20.00 (registered April 2025).
AI business users are to understand the precision and risks of AI output and confirm risk factors before use.

Run output testing (black-box end-to-end evaluation after components and mitigations are in place, reflecting real user interaction) and component testing (e.g. retrieval step in RAG, filters, system prompt) to locate failure points and catch faults masked by correct outputs.

clause_or_page: Overview table p.7; Part 3 step 2 sections 3.2-3.6 (starting pp.37, 52, 62, 73, 82)
requirement_paraphrase: Prescribes risk-specific tests: hallucination (domain knowledge, out-of-domain handling, RAG); bias (parity and counterfactual perturbation tests); undesirable content (type, ease of elicitation, helpfulness/over-refusal); data leakage (type of data, elicitation, system prompt); adversarial prompts (direct and indirect injection).

Defines methods for measuring the performance of ML models and algorithms on classification tasks; published 13 Oct 2022, 33 pages; stage 90.92; draft ISO/IEC DIS 4213 would widen scope to regression, clustering and recommendation.

clause_or_page: Outcome 4.1 / Process 4.1.1, p.29 (technical testing, generative AI)
requirement_paraphrase: Carry out regular safety and harm tests (e.g. hallucination, toxicity) using use-case-appropriate benchmarks and red-teaming, document instructions to red-teamers, test in secure environments at several lifecycle checkpoints and before deployment, have stakeholders decide whether scores are acceptable, and share results.
Providers should test algorithms before field deployment and check training data representativeness for the affected population.
For advanced AI systems, developers are to identify, evaluate and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, including before deployment.
AISI states it tests leading AI systems before they are released and collaborates with AI companies, with pre-deployment access to leading models; it open-sources evaluation tools such as Inspect.
Define, conduct and report a statistically valid analysis procedure, ideally defined in advance, that accounts for sources of variation and uncertainty and states assumptions.

Technical inspections must be conducted on autonomous vehicles; an AV must pass the technical inspection prescribed by RTA to be licensed; the Director General of RTA sets inspection types, frequency and standards by resolution.

clause_or_page: Principle 1, Build and Validate item 2, p. 14
requirement_paraphrase: Champion-model selection should include fairness metric assessment, with metrics within a threshold defined earlier for sensitive features; failures should be justified.

Conduct security risk assessments per industry standards; release models or systems only after appropriate security checks and evaluation, including benchmarking and security testing before release and verifying model/data signatures and hashes.

In addition to internal evaluations, signatories ensure qualified independent external evaluators conduct evaluations unless the model is similarly safe or safer than a reference model or no qualified evaluators can be found despite an early search; external reports or justifications go into the Model Report.
Discrimination impact assessments could be considered before release; the guideline says the timing and documentation of results and mitigations should be addressed.

Operators of AI systems whose cumulative training compute meets a threshold set by Presidential Decree must identify, assess and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, maintain an incident monitoring and response system, and submit results to the Minister.

A DPIA is required before processing likely to create high risk, and the guidance lists as triggers use of personal data in datasets used to train or refine an AI system (in the specific exception context) and profiling or automated decision-making used to decide access to a service or benefit.

Training, validation and test datasets must reflect the target population's diversity; regular data representativeness audits must be done at defined checkpoints with subgroup gaps flagged; bias detection techniques must be implemented and mitigation traceable.
Conduct a cybersecurity risk assessment that classifies AI agents' actions by potential impact, likelihood and reversibility, and apply appropriate safeguards.

Conduct adversarial testing at a regular cadence to map and measure GAI risks; evaluate performance in real-world scenarios; verify and document that structured public feedback results are incorporated in deployment go/no-go decisions.
Examine and document transparency/accountability risks; explain, validate and document the model and interpret output in context; examine and document privacy risk.

The AI Office may conduct evaluations of GPAI models to assess compliance or investigate systemic risks, may appoint independent experts, and may request access via APIs or other means including source code.
